meta.title: About Alan Belferrag — HPC & Cloud Infrastructure
meta.description: Alan Belferrag is an HPC and cloud infrastructure engineer working independently on GPU infrastructure and cloud HPC consulting.

hero.description: I’m Alan Belferrag, an HPC and cloud infrastructure engineer. I work as a Research Computing Specialist in university research computing and consult independently on GPU infrastructure and cloud HPC. My project work includes RGCP: A Self-Service GPU Compute Bridge and the design of ACC: A Production Azure HPC Platform.

whatYouGet.heading: Selected infrastructure work
whatYouGet.lead: RGCP covers GPU infrastructure and cost governance. My ParallelCluster and ACC work covers AWS delivery and Azure HPC design, while Spack Stack focuses on scientific software governance across HPC systems. Each case study explains my role and the constraints behind the work.

principles.heading: Design around the workload
principles.lead: I make infrastructure decisions around how a platform will be operated, the workloads it needs to run, and its cost limits.

items.title: Fit the operating model
items.description: Choose orchestration and automation with the size and capacity of the team operating the platform in mind.

items.title: Fit the workload mix
items.description: Account for both tightly coupled MPI jobs and memory-heavy single-node workloads when shaping the cluster and scheduler policy.

items.title: Plan for cost limits
items.description: Use capacity planning and visible usage controls rather than treating cloud compute as an unconstrained resource.

stack.title: HPC and cloud infrastructure
stack.description: My project work has involved Azure CycleCloud, Slurm, MPI, Spack, Lmod, and HyperStack, as well as cloud cluster design for research workloads.

faq.heading: Questions about my consulting work
faq.lead: A few practical details about the work and how I operate.

items.question: What does the GPU cost-reduction offer cover?
items.answer: I review GPU and model-serving spend, identify opportunities to reduce GPU or token costs, and help implement changes. The scope and savings baseline need to be agreed for each engagement.

items.question: Is there an upfront fee for that offer?
items.answer: No upfront fee for the GPU cost-reduction offer. Payment is due only after I have demonstrated real savings.

items.question: How do you establish savings?
items.answer: The method depends on the workloads and agreed scope. Before work starts, we agree on the cost baseline, comparison period, and how savings will be verified.

items.question: What GPU work have you done?
items.answer: The RGCP case study describes a self-service GPU compute platform with cost governance.

items.question: What kind of cloud HPC work do you take on?
items.answer: Cluster and cloud-compute planning and design for research-oriented organizations, including Slurm-based environments on platforms such as AWS ParallelCluster or Azure CycleCloud.

items.question: What HPC work can I review?
items.answer: The ACC case study describes my Azure HPC platform design work.

items.question: Who would I work with?
items.answer: I work independently and directly with clients. This consulting activity is separate from my day job in university research computing.

items.question: Where are you available to work?
items.answer: I’m prioritizing clients in Qatar and the GCC, and I’m open to remote clients beyond the region.

openSource.heading: Work with me directly
openSource.description: I work independently with clients. This is my personal consulting practice, not a separate company or team.

meta.title: HPC and GPU Infrastructure Consulting — Alan Belferrag
meta.description: GPU infrastructure and demonstrated-savings cost reduction for AI teams, plus cloud HPC consulting for research and engineering organizations.

hero.description: I help AI teams address GPU and token spend, and help research and engineering organizations plan cloud HPC environments.

design.heading: GPU cost reduction for AI teams
paragraphs: As an AI workload grows, GPU capacity and model-serving costs can be hard to track. I review compute use, look for ways to reduce GPU and token spend, and help put changes in place.
There’s no upfront fee for this cost-reduction offer. Payment is due only after I demonstrate real savings. The RGCP case study covers my work on self-service GPU compute and cost governance.

included.text: examine GPU and model-serving usage and establish an agreed baseline.
identify changes that could reduce GPU or token spend while taking workload needs into account.
agree the comparison method, apply the changes, and assess the demonstrated savings.

included.lead: No upfront fee for this offer
included.text: payment is due only after I demonstrate real savings.
see RGCP for an example of GPU compute provisioning and cost governance.

development.heading: Cloud HPC consulting
paragraphs: I help research and engineering teams plan cloud-compute environments around their workloads, operating capacity, security requirements, and budget. This includes Slurm-based platforms using services such as AWS ParallelCluster or Azure CycleCloud.
The ACC case study covers my design for an Azure CycleCloud-managed Slurm platform, including scheduling policy, storage, identity, budget controls, and scientific software environments.

included.text: plan the cloud HPC platform and its operational model around the organization’s needs.
consider multi-node MPI and memory-heavy single-node jobs in the Slurm design.
plan shared research storage and centrally managed scientific software where required.
account for institutional access, identity requirements, capacity limits, and cost controls.
see ACC for an example of Azure cloud HPC platform design.

performance.heading: Cost controls for compute platforms
paragraphs: Cloud platforms need clear usage limits and visibility to help prevent unplanned spend. I include capacity and cost controls in the infrastructure design instead of leaving them for a later reporting layer.
The right measures depend on the workload and operating model. RGCP and ACC show how usage limits, capacity planning, and scale-to-zero can work in different compute environments.

included.text: make compute use visible to the people responsible for cost and capacity.
consider enforceable usage limits or project budgets where appropriate.
match capacity decisions to the workload, project constraints, and expected use.
consider autoscaling or scale-to-zero for temporary and variable workloads.
for the GPU cost-reduction offer, payment is due only after demonstrated savings.

process.lead: We’ll define the workload, constraints, and scope, then agree on how to assess the work before it begins.

steps.title: Describe the workload
steps.description: Tell me what you need to run, what compute environment you use now, and what you want to change.

steps.title: Set constraints
steps.description: Clarify technical, operational, security, and cost constraints that shape the possible approach.

steps.title: Agree scope and measures
steps.description: Set the scope and, for GPU cost reduction, agree on the baseline and how we’ll verify savings.

steps.title: Review the outcome
steps.description: Evaluate the implemented design or changes against the agreed requirements and measures.

faq.heading: Questions about the work
faq.lead: The details depend on the engagement. Here’s what to expect from each service.

items.question: Is there an upfront fee?
items.answer: No upfront fee for the GPU and token cost-reduction offer. Payment is due only after I demonstrate real savings.

items.question: How will savings be demonstrated?
items.answer: The method depends on the workloads and agreed scope. Before work starts, we agree on the cost baseline, comparison period, and how savings will be verified.

items.question: What workloads are in scope?
items.answer: The offer focuses on GPU compute and model-serving costs. The specific workloads, access, and review scope need to be agreed for each engagement.

items.question: What platforms do you work with?
items.answer: My consulting focus includes cloud HPC platforms such as AWS ParallelCluster and Azure CycleCloud. The right fit depends on the organization and workload.

items.question: What kinds of organizations do you work with?
items.answer: The offer is for research-oriented organizations and engineering teams with scientific or simulation workloads.

items.question: Are you a company or agency?
items.answer: No. This is my personal, independent consulting activity. I work directly with clients; it is separate from my university role.

items.question: Where are you available?
items.answer: I operate globally without local restrictions. Based in Qatar and frequently in France/Europe, I support clients seamlessly across the GCC, Europe, and worldwide through flexible remote and hybrid setups.
